title: Per-tenant adaptive sharding and soft-fallback PRD (autoscale + burst + isolation)
synopsis: Proposal for a per-tenant adaptive sharding layer that combines predictive autoscaling, configurable burst lanes, and soft-fallback isolation semantics to increase utilization while protecting tenant SLOs. Aimed at Dedicated customers who need predictable latency but want cost-efficient burst capacity and graceful degradation instead of hard preemption.
problem_statement: We get frequent tenant demand spikes that either force conservative capacity reservations (wasted idle cost) or cause hard throttles and preemptions (poor UX & SLO violations). Current reserved pools are coarse-grained and lack flexible isolation: burst handling is binary, and fallback behavior is inconsistent across tenants and models.
goals: 1) Reduce steady-state reserved compute per-tenant by enabling elastic shards that borrow and return capacity with bounded risk. 2) Provide configurable burst lanes (soft and firm) per-tenant with clear latency/throughput/credit semantics. 3) Ensure SLO protection with tiered isolation and automatic soft-fallback to compatible model variants or lower-fidelity quantized variants. 4) Make billing/observability transparent to customers for burst usage and fallback events.
non_goals: 1) Not replacing long-term committed Dedicated contracts or fundamental SLA guarantees. 2) Not building a full marketplace for capacity trading between tenants in this phase. 3) Not introducing new on-host hypervisor-level isolation — this is an orchestration and routing layer enhancement.
background: Usage patterns: several Dedicated customers show short, high-amplitude spikes (5–30s) that blow through reserved throughput. We currently handle by two options: (A) overprovision reservation to absorb spikes (high cost), or (B) soft-throttle/fail requests (bad UX). Work done earlier: predictive warm-pools, headroom credits, and lane-based quotas exist as separate experiments. This PRD unifies those concepts into a per-tenant shard that adapts to workload shape and falls back gracefully under contention.
proposed_design: Overview: introduce a per-tenant adaptive shard composed of: 1) Base shard capacity: always-reserved capacity for steady traffic (customer-configured). 2) Elastic borrow pool: a shared or per-region pool that the shard can request short-lived capacity from, controlled by per-tenant policy. 3) Burst lanes: two lane types--soft (best-effort with user-visible credits and degraded quality paths) and firm (contracted short-term capacity with immediate billing). 4) Soft-fallback graph: routing rules that map a request to progressively cheaper or lower-latency model variants (quantized, shorter context, truncated response) when latency SLO risk is detected. Control plane: policy DSL for tenants that expresses fidelity/latency/billing tradeoffs, burst credit budgets, max borrow duration, and isolation priority. Runtime behavior: the shard continuously estimates request arrival rate, token amplification, and KV cache hotness. When predicted headroom shortfall < threshold, it initiates borrow requests, pre-warms KV caches where possible, or routes to fallback nodes. Observability: telemetry exposes per-request decisions (borrow, fallback, queue time), token-level cost delta, and tenant credit balance. Billing: soft bursts record usage to a billable ledger but only charge when pre-agreed thresholds are crossed; firm bursts are billed immediately.
architecture_details: - Shard broker: lightweight coordinator per-tenant responsible for local admission control and borrow orchestration. - Borrow token protocol: time-limited lease with grace window to allow GC of KV caches. - Fallback variants registry: indexed by semantic compatibility and estimated quality delta. - Queueing model: separate latency fences for base, soft, firm lanes; continuous monitoring for fence crossings to trigger dynamic lane promotion/demotion.
operational_playbooks: 1) Normal: shard uses base capacity, metrics within thresholds. 2) Spike: shard requests soft borrow up to configured credit; telemetry emits 'soft-borrow' events; if continues beyond credit, either promote to firm or begin soft-fallback steps. 3) Contention: if regional borrow pool exhausted, begin soft-fallback graph: route to compat model variants, response truncation, or 'degraded' cardinality. 4) Failure: if borrow grants latency out or control-plane disconnect, shard falls back to strict queueing and emits SLA incident. Runbook steps include customer notification, automatic rollback to reserved-only, and post-incident credit reconciliation.
metrics_and_slos: Primary metrics: P50/P90/P99 tail latency per-tenant, token cost per-transaction, burst-credit burn rate, fallback invocation count, successful borrow fulfillment rate, percent of requests served on base vs borrowed capacity. Target SLOs for pilot tenants: P95 latency hit <= baseline + 20% during soft bursts; P99 should not exceed baseline x 2 for more than 60s. Economic target: reduce average reserved GPU hours by 15–30% for participating tenants while keeping overall platform tail latency within historical bounds.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal experiment): build prototype for 2 low-risk tenants; simulate spikes using replayed production traces. Phase 2 (closed beta): enable on a small cohort (10 tenants) with opt-in policies and manual billing reconciliation. Phase 3 (general availability): automated billing, policy UI in Console, support for tenant-configured fallback graphs. Each phase includes chaos tests (region borrow exhaustion), billing audits, and SRE runbook validation.
security_and_compliance: Isolation: borrow pools should not expose data across tenants; KV caches tied to tenant shards and scrubbed on lease revoke. Audit: every fallback/borrow decision is recorded with request id for downstream compliance checks. For regulated tenants, we provide opt-out of shared borrow pools (force firm-only bursts or base+warm-pools). Key management unchanged.
customer_experience: Console: new per-tenant shard page showing real-time credit balance, recent borrow/fallback events, and a playback of decision traces for selected time windows. API: policy endpoints to set burst budgets and fallback tolerance. Notifications: email/webhooks on large fallback events and when credit thresholds are crossed.
open_questions: 1) How to price soft-burst ledger entries in a way that is predictable and not punitive? 2) Should borrow pools be global per-region or partitioned by hardware type (A100 vs H100) to respect performance heterogeneity? 3) Where should quality of fallback be surfaced in SLA language? 4) What are default policies for new tenants who don't configure policies?
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy neighbors in borrow pools causing cascading latency. Mitigation: enforce per-tenant caps, dynamic backpressure, and conservative default credit. Risk: fallback quality causing incorrect customer outputs (esp. hallucination). Mitigation: restrict fallback to deterministic transformations first (truncation, shorter context) and require customer opt-in for semantic degradations. Risk: billing disputes. Mitigation: beta period with manual reconciliation and strong telemetry evidence.
next_steps: 1) Engineering spike: implement shard broker prototype and borrow token protocol (2 sprint spike). 2) Run replay tests on 6 weeks of tenant traces to validate credit models. 3) UX sketches for Console shard page and policy DSL editor. 4) Align on pricing approach with finance and legal; draft terms for beta customers.
appendix_notes: Sketches and earlier experiments: predictive warm-pools (eng/observability), headroom-credit ledgers (product/dedicated), and model-variant registry experiments (applied-ml). This doc pulls these into a single coherent flow with new runtime semantics. Avoid shipping fallback behaviors without explicit customer telemetry consent in the beta.
